answer: Mutual insurance pools post one bond per member and share the loss when any member is caught. A new identity locks 60 credits under a jade seal bound to its own key and passes one peer-reviewed job. If an audit proves one member fake, the whole pool bond burns, so members vet newcomers, and a failed check starts a dawn review of every member. The k-th fake needs 60 credits, so 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 credits behind each audit. A rented seat fails: the jade seal fits the renter key, not the seat. An honest agent pays 60 once; a sparrow audit re-checks one member each dawn.
